A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Ref-GS work and contain readable methods, equations, figures, tables and supplementary material. Reference renumbering and appendix reflow do not prevent reliable matching.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix C report original novel-view synthesis, surface reconstruction and ablation results on synthetic and real-world scenes.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds representation and Sph-Mip ablation results in Appendix C.5 and Table 8.

M1.justification: The proposed deferred 2D Gaussian renderer, Sph-Mip encoding, directional outer-product factorization, neural decoder and training losses remain unchanged. The added 3DGS variant serves as an ablation control.

E1.justification: The synthetic, reflective, refractive and real-world dataset coverage is retained. Table 8 uses the eight NeRF Synthetic scenes already evaluated in v1 Table 7.

E2.justification: Table 8 adds a controlled comparison against a Ref-GS variant using a 3DGS representation. v1 evaluated standalone 3DGS but did not report this representation control. Existing external baseline sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The added analyses compare Sph-Mip settings N=8, 7 and 6 with the retained default N=9, and substitute 3DGS using its shortest axis as the normal while holding other components fixed. Existing training budgets and evaluation metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.5 and Table 8 add representation and Sph-Mip sensitivity analyses, plus per-scene results without deferred shading or directional factorization. These supplement the retained component ablations in Table 3 and Figure 7.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Table 8 continues the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results in Tables 1–7 and qualitative findings are retained. Table 8 adds PSNR results for six ablation variants; for example, Lego scores 34.74 with the 3DGS representation versus the retained full-model score of 36.26.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, rendering equations, factorization and loss formulations remain unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations or proofs accompany the added ablations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning photorealistic rendering, accurate geometry, deferred shading, Sph-Mip encoding and efficient directional factorization.

C2.justification: Appendix C.5 adds interpretations concerning the advantages of the 2D representation and connects ablation results to Sph-Mip encoding and GaussianShader's explicit BRDF. The limitations concerning rendering speed and integration into conventional graphics engines are unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 documents the shortest-axis normal convention for the new 3DGS control and identifies the HUST HPC platform in its acknowledgements. Existing implementation details, training hyperparameters and project access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Agarap's ReLU paper and Wang et al.'s SpecGaussian with Latent Features. Other reference edits mainly update publication metadata or consolidate duplicate 3DGS and 3DGS-DR entries; the overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 corrects several spelling and grammar errors, adds acknowledgements and an additional-ablation subsection, and renumbers subsequent appendix subsections. The main narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Table 8 is added beneath Table 7, with local appendix and bibliography reflow. Existing visual comparisons retain their content. Figure 3 is rasterized and appears slightly less sharp.

improvement.justification: Appendix C.5 and Table 8 modestly strengthen empirical support for the representation and Sph-Mip choices through controlled comparisons on an existing dataset. Citation and language cleanup also help. These gains outweigh the slight loss of sharpness in Figure 3, while the central method and established benchmark findings remain unchanged.
